title: Mentoring an Intern
paragraphs: When assigned to mentor a nervous new intern fresh out of university, Layla remembered her own difficult first months at the company, when nobody had taken the time to explain unwritten expectations clearly.

Rather than simply assigning tasks and expecting the intern to figure things out independently, Layla scheduled brief daily check-ins specifically to answer questions the intern might feel embarrassed to ask openly in meetings.
During one such check-in, the intern admitted he had been silently struggling with a particular software tool for days, too afraid of appearing incompetent to ask for help earlier.

Layla reassured him that asking questions early prevented far larger problems later, and spent an extra hour that afternoon walking him through the tool step by step until he felt genuinely confident.
By the end of his three-month internship, the same intern had become one of the more confident members of the team, frequently helping other new interns who joined after him.
Layla later reflected that investing time in mentorship rarely shows immediate results, but consistently pays off months later in ways that are easy to overlook if not actively observed.
